The outlined treatment plan for Grace's osteoarthritis is highly appropriate and aligns with standard clinical guidelines. Osteoarthritis management typically focuses on symptom relief and improving joint function without invasive procedures. Over-the-counter pain relievers (such as acetaminophen or NSAIDs) are first-line pharmacological interventions for mild to moderate pain. Low-impact aerobic exercises like swimming and biking are recommended because they maintain cardiovascular health and joint mobility while minimizing stress on the knee joints. Furthermore, physical therapy aimed at strengthening the quadriceps and other muscles surrounding the knee is crucial, as stronger muscles provide better support and stability to the joint, thereby reducing pain and slowing disease progression. This multimodal approach addresses both pain management and functional improvement, which is the cornerstone of conservative osteoarthritis care.
